findings.summary: High-contrast support and link differentiation are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The preference probe found no forced-colors or prefers-contrast rules. Lighthouse found four homepage and two registration links distinguishable only by low-contrast colour, including a 1.41:1 link-versus-surrounding-text contrast.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast handling, preserve system colors, and distinguish inline links with an underline or another non-colour cue.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly with no View Transition or attention cue.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection across the MPA templates found no @view-transition or view-transition-name use; screenshots show separate routes with no continuity mechanism.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-origin cross-document View Transitions with a reduced-motion fallback and stable names for shared header/content elements.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state feedback or progress affordance.
findings.evidence: The long homepage and FAQ screenshots show static chrome; CSS inspection contains no scroll-state container queries, progress indicator, or scroll-position-aware treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress/position affordance on long listing and FAQ pages, preferably declaratively and without scroll event work.

findings.summary: A bright promotional banner precedes the core content on every audited template.
findings.evidence: Every route screenshot begins with a full-width red “FREE MEGA links” promotion before the site header, with no dismiss control.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the site-wide interruption or move the promotion after primary content; if it must persist, make it clearly labelled and dismissible with remembered state.

findings.summary: The mobile navigation is a pointer-only custom div instead of a semantic disclosure/popover.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM uses a clickable div with inline onclick to toggle another div; it has no button semantics, expanded state, or native popover/details light-dismiss behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real button controlling a popover or details element, expose aria-expanded/controls as needed, and retain Escape/light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Reusable galleries adapt only through viewport media queries, not their containers.
findings.evidence: The shared CSS has a single max-width media query and no @container/container-type, while the same .recot/.reco gallery component is reused in multiple layout contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Give gallery/list wrappers containment and use container queries for tile sizing and density so embedded instances adapt independently.

findings.summary: Touch targets and controls are substantially smaller than accessible target sizes.
findings.evidence: The keyboard/target probe measured many links at 13px high and registration fields at about 18px high; mobile screenshots confirm tightly packed icon and text targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas toward at least 44x44 CSS px, add spacing, and keep a visible :focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: Registration errors are cryptic and are not programmatically connected to their fields.
findings.evidence: Submitting an empty registration shows “username should only contain 4 to 16 aphanumeric latin symbols” beside the login field, but the DOM has no required, aria-invalid, aria-describedby, or live error announcement.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, use specific plain-language messages, mark invalid fields, connect descriptions with aria-describedby, and announce the error summary.

findings.summary: The homepage LCP misses the good Core Web Vitals threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 2.9s and the independent trace measured 3.906s; good LCP is 2.5s or less. CLS was only 0.016 and TBT effectively zero.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a correctly sized hero variant, preserve fetchpriority, reduce font/network competition, and verify LCP under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is extremely heavy and poorly cached for a thumbnail-led homepage.
findings.evidence: The HAR transferred 12.64MB across 67 requests; Lighthouse measured 14,547KiB. A single Material Symbols font was 3.74MB, and cache analysis estimated 6,592KiB savings across 64 resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset/self-host icons, deliver thumbnail-sized image variants with srcset/sizes, set durable immutable caching for versioned media, and avoid loading below-fold originals.

findings.summary: Analytics JavaScript is mostly unused on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 52–53KiB of unused JavaScript from Yandex Metrika on both homepage and registration templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Load analytics only after consent/idle or replace it with a smaller privacy-preserving measurement endpoint.

findings.summary: Registration fields have no programmatic labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed both login and email inputs for missing labels; the DOM probe confirmed labels=null and aria-label=null for each field.
findings.suggestedFix: Use explicit <label for> elements and stable input ids; retain visible labels rather than relying on adjacent spans.

findings.summary: Pages lack semantic landmarks and navigation structure.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports no main landmark on homepage and registration; the registration probe found no main, nav, header, footer, aside, or explicit role landmarks.
findings.suggestedFix: Use header/nav/main/footer landmarks and ensure the mobile menu trigger participates in keyboard order with a visible focus state.

findings.summary: Mobile typography is cramped and truncates important context.
findings.evidence: Mobile CSS sets body text to 3vw, about 10.8px at 360px, while screenshots show a clipped registration title and heavily truncated gallery labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a rem/clamp-based minimum near 16px for body text, allow headings to wrap, and reserve truncation for non-essential metadata with an accessible full name.

findings.summary: Images lack intrinsic dimensions and responsive source sizing.
findings.evidence: The image audit found all 61 rendered images missing complete width/height dimensions and all 61 lacking img srcset; 49 were more than twice their rendered width.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or aspect-ratio for every image and provide srcset/sizes that select thumbnail, card, and hero-sized files.

findings.summary: Chrome reports platform hygiene problems, including BFCache blockers.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found DevTools Inspector issues on both templates and five BFCache failure reasons on registration.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the reported Inspector issue and BFCache blockers, then retest navigation restoration; avoid unnecessary unload-sensitive third-party behavior.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap indexing signals are inconsistent across public templates.
findings.evidence: Homepage has a canonical and valid hreflang, but search and registration heads have no canonical. /sitemap.xml returns 410 while robots.txt points to two .txt sitemap resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Add self-referential canonicals to indexable templates, serve a conventional sitemap index (or clearly valid text sitemaps), and keep robots/sitemap status consistent.

findings.summary: Rich entity and share-preview metadata is absent.
findings.evidence: Homepage and public content DOM contain descriptive title/meta but no Open Graph metadata or JSON-LD for the organization, image gallery, or photo entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter image previews and appropriate schema.org Organization/ImageObject or CollectionPage JSON-LD matching visible content.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security policy is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers confirm HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, and X-Frame-Options DENY, but Content-Security-Policy and Permissions-Policy are missing; Referrer-Policy is the permissive legacy no-referrer-when-downgrade.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP (prefer nonces/hashes), a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy, and lengthen HSTS after validation.

findings.summary: Yandex analytics tracks users on load without an observed consent gate.
findings.evidence: Network evidence shows Yandex Metrika starts immediately, makes redirecting cookie-sync/watch requests, and Lighthouse found 15–16 third-party cookies. The cookie audit also found three SameSite=None analytics cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not load non-essential analytics before informed consent; minimize events and identifiers, disable cookie sync/session-wide tracking, and consider first-party aggregate measurement.

findings.summary: Account creation relies on emailed passwords rather than modern authentication.
findings.evidence: The registration copy states “We will send your password to this email”; audited auth/account surfaces expose no WebAuthn/passkey path.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace emailed reusable passwords with verified email links and offer passkey registration/authentication, with appropriate reauthentication for sensitive account actions.

findings.summary: Bilingual templates use physical CSS properties rather than writing-mode-safe logical properties.
findings.evidence: Pages correctly expose lang=en and en/ru/x-default hreflang, but shared CSS is dominated by left/right, width/height, margin-left and padding-right with no logical-property strategy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir explicitly where needed and migrate reusable layout spacing/sizing to margin/padding/inset-inline/block and inline-size/block-size.

findings.summary: Registration inputs do not provide browser input assistance.
findings.evidence: The login and email inputs have no autocomplete tokens; email is type=text and neither field supplies required or inputmode hints.
findings.suggestedFix: Use type=email, autocomplete=email and username tokens, required, and suitable inputmode/autocapitalize settings.

findings.summary: Oversized media and font payloads are disproportionate to the rendered thumbnail grid.
findings.evidence: 49 of 61 images were over 2x rendered width; homepage transfers 8.76MB of images plus a 3.74MB icon font, while most cards display at only about 129px.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate small AVIF/WebP thumbnails, add width descriptors and sizes, lazy-load strictly below-fold media, and replace/subset the multi-megabyte icon font.
